new_statements.quote: ...dialectos quechuas que ofrecen un patrón acentual reminiscente del descrito por el gramático mencionado figuran, según Torero, el ancashino (cf., en efecto, Parker 1967) y las hablas de Cajatambo y Chancay (Lima); a ellos pueden agregarse también las variedades de Ferreñafe (Escribens 1977: 50-53) y Amazonas (Taylor 1975: 36-37). En éstas la carga culminativa depende de la posición y del carácter constitutivo de las sílabas dentro de la palabra. De esta manera, lo que distingue a tales dialectos de los demás es que en ellos la sílaba inicial puede portar el rasgo culminativo, si reúne las condiciones: hecho inusitado en el resto de las variedades en donde prima la acentuación penúltima.
new_statements.translation: ...Quechua dialects showing an accentual pattern reminiscent of the one described by the aforementioned grammarian [Domingo de Santo Tomás] include, according to Torero, Ancash Quechua (cf. indeed Parker 1967) and the varieties of Cajatambo and Chancay (Lima); to these may be added Ferreñafe (Escribens 1977: 50-53) and Amazonas (Taylor 1975: 36-37). In these the culminative (stress) load depends on the position and on the make-up of the syllables within the word. Thus what sets these dialects apart from the rest is that in them the initial syllable can carry the culminative feature, if it meets the conditions — something unheard-of in the other varieties, where penultimate accentuation prevails.
new_statements.citation: Cerrón-Palomino, Rodolfo. 1987. Lingüística quechua. Cusco: Centro de Estudios Rurales Andinos 'Bartolomé de Las Casas', cap. IV sec. 4.5 (el acento); reporting Torero 1964:461. Corroborated by Adelaar & Muysken 2004:207.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Unlike general Quechua penultimate stress, Cajatambo (with Chancay/Huaral and Ancash) has stress placement conditioned by syllable position and syllable structure (weight), such that the word-initial syllable may take primary stress when the conditions are met; Adelaar & Muysken 2004:207 gloss the same facts as 'word-initial stress and stress dependent on syllable structure... in QI Ancash and in QI Cajatambo (cf. Torero 1964: 461)'. The explicit conditions are not given in the accessible text; the Ancash analogue (Parker 1976:58-59) is: stress the non-final heavy (closed or long-vowel) syllable, otherwise the initial syllable, in clause-final/citation forms.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Cerrón-Palomino's dialectology chapter (snippet, gbfeed_cp1987_o/e.xml): '...primera sílaba con un acento secundario que recae en la penúltima, cuando la palabra contiene más de tres sílabas. Tales dialectos, entre los que caben mencionar a las hablas de Cajatambo y Chancay (Lima), Ancash, Ferreñafe (Lambayeque) y...' — i.e. primary stress on the first syllable with a secondary stress on the penult in words of more than three syllables (the words immediately preceding 'primera sílaba' fall in a snippet gap).
new_statements.exceptions: None visible for Cajatambo specifically; the general-Quechua statement in the same passage is 'el acento de intensidad recae sobre la penúltima sílaba de la palabra' with these dialects as the exception. Parker 1976 (Ancash analogue) notes final stress in interjections and on word-final long syllables (1st-person length).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level culminative stress; Cerrón-Palomino speaks of 'la palabra'. Parker's Ancash description, which both secondary sources pair with Cajatambo, distinguishes clause-final (incl. citation) forms from clause-medial forms; whether Torero 1964 makes the same distinction for Cajatambo could not be checked.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statements concern 'las hablas de Cajatambo' = the Quechua of Cajatambo province (upper Pativilca, dept. Lima), i.e. caja1239 / ISO qvl proper; Cerrón-Palomino groups it with Chancay (Huaral province, North Lima; Glottolog chan1318-area varieties) and Ancash-Huaylas (huay1240). Note Glottolog/UNESCO alt-names for caja1239 ('Yaru, Tarma, Junín') reflect a broader 'Cajatambo–Pasco–N Junín' lumping; the accent statement applies to Cajatambo province speech only, not to Yaru/Tarma. Pacaraos (paca1245), also North Lima, has a different, partly phonemic stress system and is not covered by this statement.

sources.note: After Torero: Ancash (Parker) and 'las hablas de Cajatambo y Chancay (Lima)' (plus Ferreñafe, Amazonas) have an accent pattern where culminative stress depends on position and syllable make-up, so the initial syllable can bear main stress 'si reúne las condiciones', unlike the penultimate norm elsewhere; second passage: '...primera sílaba con un acento secundario que recae en la penúltima, cuando la palabra contiene más de tres sílabas' for Cajatambo, Chancay, Ancash, Ferreñafe. Page numbers not visible in snippets.

sources.note: Describes Ancash: penultimate in most of Ancash; in Callejón de Huaylas clause-final words stress the non-final long syllable, else the initial syllable; clause-medial words stress the initial. Does not mention Cajatambo (checked by grep) — it is the Ancash analogue Adelaar and Cerrón-Palomino pair with Cajatambo.
